questions.prompt: Which statement is a hypothesis rather than a topic or question?
options: Why is SLAM hard? which asks for an explanation rather than a testable, measurable claim.
Does fusion reduce drift? which poses a question without any prediction or threshold given.
Robot grasping in clutter, a research area that names no claim, metric or comparison at all.
Fusing wheel odometry cuts final position error by 20% or more on three warehouse logs versus lidar-only SLAM.
questions.explanation: Only the last names an intervention, comparison, metric, population and minimum effect.

questions.prompt: Run-to-run sd is 6 and the minimum effect is 4. How many runs per method (5% level, 80% power, round up)?
If the minimum effect halves (and sd stays the same), by what factor does the required number of runs change?
questions.explanation: n is proportional to 1/delta^2, so halving delta multiplies n by 4.

questions.prompt: With power raised to 90% (z = 1.96 + 1.28 = 3.24) instead of 80% (z = 2.8), sd 3 and minimum effect 2, how many runs per method (round up)?
questions.skillLabel: Effect of power on sample size

questions.prompt: Idea keywords {event, camera, slam, dynamic}; prior work {event, camera, slam, static, outdoor}. What is the novelty score 1 - Jaccard? Give 2 decimals.
Five baseline runs give failure rates 10, 12, 11, 13, 12 and the new method gives 8, 9, 8, 10, 9. What is the mean reduction (baseline minus new)?

Five baseline runs give failure rates 10, 12, 11, 13, 12 and the new method gives 8, 9, 8, 10, 9. What is the lower end of the 95% CI of the reduction (baseline minus new), using the Welch standard error and t = 2.776? Give 2 decimals.
questions.explanation: Variances 1.3 and 0.7; SE = sqrt(0.26+0.14) = 0.632; half-width 1.756; lower end 2.8 - 1.756 = 1.04.

questions.prompt: With a minimum effect of 2 points and an interval of [1.04, 4.56] for the reduction, what is the decision?
options: Supported, because the interval excludes zero and so the reduction is real.
Rejected, because the lower end of the interval is below the minimum effect of 2.
Inconclusive: the interval straddles the minimum effect, so more runs are needed.
Supported, because the mean of the interval is above the minimum effect of 2.
questions.explanation: Supported needs the lower end at or above 2; rejected needs the upper end below 2; neither holds.

questions.prompt: Which plan has a forking-path problem?
options: Report all pre-declared metrics with intervals.
Fix the metric, maps and number of runs, then run once and report.
Run the experiment, then pick the metric and maps where the method looks best.
State the exclusion rule before collecting data.
questions.explanation: Choosing analysis details after seeing results inflates false positives.

questions.prompt: Your method beats the default baseline but not a simple tuned heuristic. What can you conclude?
options: The method is the state of the art, since it beats the baseline that most papers use as a reference.
The gain over the default may come from tuning, not your idea; it is not shown against the stronger baseline.
The tuned heuristic must be cheating, since a simple rule should not beat a learned method at all.
Baselines are irrelevant to novelty, which depends only on the new method itself.
questions.explanation: Beating only a weak baseline is weak evidence.

questions.prompt: Choose four comparisons for a learned grasp-pose predictor and say what each one tests.
rubric: Includes the default method and a strong simple/heuristic baseline with equal tuning effort.
Includes an ablation of the claimed ingredient and optionally an oracle upper bound.
Says what a win against each one would show or rule out.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: A pilot gives a 3.8-point reduction with CI [1.7, 5.9] and your pre-registered minimum effect is 5. Explain what you conclude, and what you do next.
rubric: Concludes inconclusive: neither supported nor rejected.
Next: run the pre-registered sample size or compute runs needed from the observed sd.
Does not change the threshold or metric after seeing the data (or labels any change as exploratory).
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: A decide() function returns 'supported' for a CI of [-0.5, 6] with minimum effect 5. Find the likely bug and give a test that would catch it.
rubric: Identifies that it compares the point estimate or upper bound rather than the lower bound with the minimum effect.
Fix: supported only if lower >= min_effect.
Test: CI [-0.5, 6] with min_effect 5 must return inconclusive.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
